status: exploratory follow-up; frozen before inspecting learning-curve results
question: How does a simulation-score predictor improve as more evaluated training-policy groups become available?
source: same pinned 25 cotrain RoboTwin configurations, 50 known tasks, and 17 ancestry-proxy groups as robotwin_plan.json
outer_folds: unchanged original 3 family-grouped folds x 3 seeded partitions
anchors: fixed 10 same-condition tasks; original five anchor draws; same targets at every training size
subsampling: five score-independent random group orders per outer fold; select ceil(fraction * available_groups), at least two; nested subsets; keep all policies of selected groups
inner_tuning: original latent rank/ridge search rerun inside each selected training subset; no outer test target enters selection
predictors: all seven original methods unchanged; chart Latent, Additive, Scale and AnchorMean
endpoints: family-macro MAE and task-macro ranking error at observed gap >= 0.10; predicted ties cost 0.5; both policies jointly held out
aggregation: average training subset draws and repeated designs within policy then family for MAE; pool disjoint folds then average designs within task for ranking
uncertainty: 2000 paired bootstrap draws over group proxies for MAE or tasks for ranking; descriptive only, no independent-trial interpretation
x_axis: mean training policy-task score cells per fit, excluding held-out policy anchors; exact policy/group/cell ranges retained
limits: training data means published evaluation scores used by the meta-predictor, not robot-policy demonstrations; no new tasks, physical validation, power-law fit, or extrapolation beyond observed budgets
